wrong_belief: AI is magic or a living creature like an animal.
correction: AI is not magic and it is not alive. People build AI with computers and teach it using examples and steps.
citation: Grade 3 · Unit 1 · Smart or Not? · p.4

wrong_belief: Any machine with a battery or motor, like a ceiling fan or toy car, uses AI.
correction: Machines like fans and battery toy cars only repeat the same mechanical motion. AI machines notice information from sensors and learn or decide.
citation: Grade 3 · Unit 1 · Smart or Not? · p.4

wrong_belief: Computers have human eyes and ears inside them.
correction: Computers use electronic sensors. Cameras act like eyes, microphones like ears, and touchscreens like skin.
citation: Grade 3 · Unit 2 · How Machines Sense · p.6

wrong_belief: AI programs always need humans to write a separate rule for every single dog or cat picture.
correction: Rule-based machines need explicit rules, but machine learning allows computers to find features on their own from many training examples.
citation: Grade 4 · Unit 1 · Rules or Learning? · p.4

wrong_belief: If an AI makes a mistake, it means the computer is broken.
correction: AI mistakes usually happen because the training data was too small, missing examples, or biased.
citation: Grade 4 · Unit 7 · When AI Gets It Wrong · p.16

wrong_belief: A computer sees an image the same way a human sees people and shapes.
correction: A computer only sees a grid of numbers representing pixels and color intensities. It detects edges and features mathematically.

wrong_belief: If a video or photo looks real on the internet, it must be real.
correction: Generative AI can create realistic deepfakes. Always verify with the STOP framework (Source, Think, Other sources, Pause).
citation: Grade 5 · Unit 7 · Fact or Fake? · p.16

wrong_belief: AI systems can understand everything about the world like humans do.
correction: Current AI is Narrow AI (ANI) trained on specific domains and tasks. It does not have general human intelligence or feelings.
citation: Grade 6 · Unit 1 · What Makes AI Intelligent? · p.4

wrong_belief: Computers are completely unbiased and objective by nature.
correction: If training data contains historical human biases or misses certain groups, the AI model will learn and repeat that bias.
citation: Grade 6 · Unit 8 · AI Ethics: Privacy and Bias · p.18

wrong_belief: Chatbots understand the true meaning and feelings of words when they reply.
correction: Chatbots perform tokenisation and statistical prediction of the most likely next tokens based on language patterns, without human consciousness.
citation: Grade 7 · Unit 2 · Natural Language Processing · p.6

wrong_belief: Supervised and unsupervised learning are the exact same thing.
correction: Supervised learning uses labeled data with inputs and known target answers. Unsupervised learning finds natural clusters in unlabeled data.
citation: Grade 7 · Unit 4 · Supervised vs Unsupervised · p.10

wrong_belief: Accuracy is the only metric you need to know if a machine learning model is good.
correction: When classes are imbalanced (e.g. rare disease detection), high accuracy can be misleading. Precision, Recall, and F1 score are essential.

wrong_belief: Artificial neural networks work exactly like the biological human brain.
correction: Artificial neural networks are mathematical abstractions inspired by biological neurons, using linear weights, biases, and activation functions.

wrong_belief: A model that scores 100% on the training set is a perfect model.
correction: 100% training score often indicates overfitting, where the model memorized noise and fails to generalize to unseen test data.
citation: Grade 9 · Unit 5 · Neural Networks in Depth · p.12

wrong_belief: Large language models are search engines that always cite verified facts from memory.
correction: LLMs generate plausible text based on probabilities, which can lead to confident hallucinations unless grounded via RAG and verified sources.
citation: Grade 10 · Unit 6 · How LLMs Work · p.14
